correctness.rationale: Upper bound is valid: Petersen 1-factor theorem for bridgeless cubic graphs (cited classical theorem, not re-proved) implies any independent set meets each matched edge at most once, so alpha(G) <= n/2 for every admissible G. Lower bounds independently re-verified from witnesses.json edge lists only with a separate implementation: all 7 witnesses are simple (no loops/duplicate edges), exactly 3-regular with 3n/2 edges, connected, bridgeless (Tarjan, 0 bridges), bipartite, girth exactly as claimed (12-g4=4, 14-g4=4, 14-g6=6, 16-g4=4, 16-g6=6, 18-g4=4, 18-g6=6), and carry an explicit independent set of size n/2. Brute-force cross-check on n=12 prism gives alpha=6, confirming equality not just >=. Hence for each claimed cell M(n,g) >= n/2 and <= n/2, so = n/2. Boundaries honest: (12,6) emptiness via (3,6)-cage order 14 is correct classical fact and no witness is offered; girth-3 sampling bests and girth-5 observations are explicitly labeled as computed evidence/conjectures with no optimality claimed; abandoned exhaustive generation is disclosed and plays no role in the proof. Proof versus experiment is correctly distinguished.

originality.rationale: No prior publishes the stated M(n,g)=max-alpha table for cubic bridgeless 12-18 as a maximum with proof. Nearest priors are substantively different invariants: Balogh-Kostochka-Liu (arXiv:1708.03996) bounds asymptotic infimum i(3,infinity)<=0.454; Perarnau-Perkins (arXiv:1611.01474) proves counting/independence-polynomial extremality of Heawood/Petersen unions; Dvorak-Sereni-Volec (arXiv:1301.5296) proves universal fractional-chromatic 14/5 lower bound (alpha/n>=5/14). None defines or implies per-order exact maxima M(n,g) or a separated gap witness for this window. The witness graphs themselves are classical (prisms, Heawood, GP(8,3)/Moebius-Kantor, Pappus-type) and the two textbook lemmas used are classical, so mechanical implication is a value defect, not a prior-publication defeat; no identical table with maximality certificate was found. Priority is decided by substantive comparison, not by timestamp or failed search.

value.rationale: The 7-cell headline M(n,g)=n/2 is a textbook restatement / mechanically implied ceiling, even if correct and narrowly new as a table. For any (n,g) cell containing one bipartite bridgeless cubic graph, M=n/2 follows in one line: bipartite partite set gives alpha>=n/2; Petersen matching gives alpha<=n/2 for every cell member. The entire content therefore reduces to existence of a bipartite example per cell. Five cells are classical existence: (12,4)/(16,4) hexagonal/octagonal prisms (infinite bipartite prism family, m even); (14,6) Heawood unique (3,6)-cage; (16,6) GP(8,3)=Moebius-Kantor (n even, k odd => bipartite, girth 6); (18,6) 18-vertex bipartite cubic girth 6 (Pappus graph is the textbook 18-vertex cubic bipartite girth-6 example; the committed ring-plus-offset-5 graph is the same stratum). The remaining two witnesses (14,4)/(18,4) are explicitly disclaimed as arbitrary computer-found adjacency data with no canonicity, novelty, or mathematical interpretation claimed. No separated integer gap exists by the authors' own admission (all maxima hit the n/2 ceiling; ties are the rule), so the original gap-witness target failed; no complete M(n,g) table was delivered (girth 3 and 5 explicitly unclaimed). No conjecture is tested, no heuristic needs this precise tabulation beyond consulting standard cage/prism references, and the B&B pipeline is admittedly unused for the final upper bounds. Per the standard, a narrow exact datum can pass only when motivated before computation, not mechanically implied, and reasonably retrievable later; here the value is mechanically implied by cited 1891 + bipartite facts plus known graphs, and certification alone does not rescue arbitrary objects. This is intrinsic low value, not a fixable presentation defect.
